The Partons were so poor that Dolly’s father had to pay the doctor who attended her birth with a sack of cornmeal. pinboard.title: Ads and tracking infiltrated TVs. Now they're coming for monitors • Ars Technica
pinboard.description:
Scharon Harding:

Beyond the LG debacle, there’s a broader concern that monitors are being turned into ad-pushing trackers: smart monitors. Smart monitors connect to the Internet and run their own operating system (OS) and apps. They can be useful for performing tasks, like video conferencing, watching a show from a streaming service, or managing your smart home without attaching a computer. LG’s and Samsung’s smart monitors use the same ad-serving OSes that their respective smart TVs do, meaning they’re poised to use automatic content recognition (ACR). Users of LG and Samsung smart monitors, including reviews site RTINGs, have shown the displays being able to track user activity. I asked LG and Samsung if their smart monitors use ACR and will update this article if I get any responses. When using a smart monitor, you not only have to worry about what the monitor could be tracking, but also what the OS operator (such as Google for Android-powered smart monitors) and third-party app providers (such as Netflix) can track. That’s a lot of lengthy policy text to parse in order to understand what exactly your smart monitor is tracking and how that data may be used. For the record, the privacy policies for monitors by companies LG, Samsung, and Acer (Acer also makes smart monitors) all state that the companies may share data collected from its devices with advertisers. There are reasons for smart monitors to exist beyond their potential for ads and tracking: there’s genuine demand for them, including among people with limited spaces seeking simplified, sharable computing solutions. But smart TVs also had a logical, consumer-friendly purpose before the industry started pumping them with ads.

And the problem with monitors is that unlike (smart) TVs you can't keep them disconnected from the internet.
